name: Solar Power Plant
outcome: Clean electricity for the campus; see live solar statistics
summary: The 235 kWp solar installation has three plants (15, 100 and 120 kWp) and is the largest contributor to the institution's clean-energy profile. The 120 kWp plant was commissioned on 22 April 2026. Monthly generation, KSEB import and the solar share are on the solar statistics page.
does: Generates clean, renewable energy on campus
Reduces the carbon footprint of the institution
note: kWp is the peak (DC) rating of the installed panels.
basis: Renewable share of energy (target 7.2) and lower carbon emissions (13.2). Secondary: clean infrastructure (9.4), less air pollution (3.9, 11.6), and the plant as a learning resource (4.7).

co2.basis: KSEB data supplied by the institution
co2.label: 150 to 200 t

name: Sewage Treatment Plant
outcome: Treated water for safe discharge and reuse
summary: The sewage treatment plant has a capacity of 50,000 litres per day and treats campus waste water for safe discharge and reuse. It includes an aerobic upflow filter, a tertiary settling tank and a filter feed tank.
basis: Treatment and safe reuse of waste water (6.3). Secondary: less pollution reaching water bodies and soil (14.1, 12.4) and fewer water-borne health risks (3.9).

co2.basis: 50 to 80% of 50 m³ per day reused, replacing fresh water at about 0.5 kWh per m³
co2.label: 2.6 to 5.2 t (gross)

name: Rainwater Harvesting
summary: The rainwater harvesting system has a stated capacity of 11 Lakh litres (1.1 million litres), collecting roof rainwater and recharging groundwater.
basis: Water-use efficiency and groundwater recharge (6.4, 6.6). Secondary: climate adaptation and resilience to dry spells (13.1) and protection of groundwater-dependent ecosystems (15.1).

co2.basis: 1 to 3 tank fills per year (1,100 to 3,300 m³) at about 0.5 kWh per m³
co2.label: 0.4 to 1.2 t

name: Bio-Gas Plant
outcome: Organic waste converted to cooking gas
summary: The 41 m³ bio-gas plant converts organic waste into clean cooking gas, cutting waste and improving soil health.
does: Converts organic waste to clean energy
Reduces waste and improves soil health
basis: Clean cooking fuel (7.1) and waste reduction and recycling (12.5). Secondary: lower methane emissions from organic waste (13.2), soil health from the slurry (15.3) and campus waste management (11.6).

co2.basis: 20 to 41 m³ of gas per day replacing LPG (0.43 kg LPG per m³; 2.9 kg CO₂ per kg LPG)
co2.label: 9 to 19 t
